lines.trans: Two mint teas and three lemon tarts for table four under the lemon tree!
Coming right up! Tomas, take the hot teapot to the corner table!

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: At table two they say this almond crust is the best pastry on Calle de los Tilos!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: Tell table two the secret was my two Wednesday kitchen apprentices!
How many slices of lemon tart are left on tray four, Rocio?
Count them: one, two, three... out of forty slices in fifteen minutes!
Good thing you baked two extra trays of warm cinnamon rolls just in case!
Listen: the room just went quiet! Someone is tapping a music stand!
Our neighbour from number ten brought his violin case into Room Nine!
Leave the clean plates for five minutes, both of you, and come listen at the door!
Save those last three slices of tart for Carmen, Mateo, and Ernesto!
Aprons off: it is six o'clock on Friday!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

Coming right up! Tomas, take the hot teapot to the corner table!

lines.trans: Two mint teas and three lemon tarts for table four under the lemon tree!
Coming right up! Tomas, take the hot teapot to the corner table!

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: At table two they say this almond crust is the best pastry on Calle de los Tilos!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

How many slices of lemon tart are left on tray four, Rocio?
Count them: one, two, three... out of forty slices in fifteen minutes!
Good thing you baked two extra trays of warm cinnamon rolls just in case!

Leave the clean plates for five minutes, both of you, and come listen at the door!
Save those last three slices of tart for Carmen, Mateo, and Ernesto!
Aprons off: it is six o'clock on Friday!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

acaso.gloss: perhaps; by chance (por si acaso = just in case)

meanings.en: perhaps; by chance (por si acaso = just in case)
meanings.note: Most common in everyday speech inside the fixed phrase por si acaso ('just in case').

examples.text: Llevo un paraguas pequeño por si acaso llueve.
examples.trans: I carry a small umbrella just in case it rains.

examples.text: Horneamos otra bandeja de pan por si acaso vienen más vecinos.
examples.trans: We baked another tray of bread just in case more neighbours come.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.

examples.text: ¿Hay alguien en recepción?
examples.trans: Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

meanings.note: Final -z changes to -c- before -es in the plural (aprendices); feminine singular can be la aprendiz or la aprendiza.

examples.text: El joven aprendiz prepara la masa del pan cada mañana.
examples.trans: The young apprentice prepares the bread dough every morning.

examples.text: Mis dos aprendices de cocina trabajaron de maravilla el miércoles.
examples.trans: My two kitchen apprentices worked wonderfully on Wednesday.

meanings.note: Wooden or metal rest that holds sheet music open.

examples.text: Pon la hoja de música sobre el atril del piano.
examples.trans: Put the sheet of music on the piano's music stand.

examples.text: El atril de nogal se pliega hacia dentro.
examples.trans: The walnut music stand folds inward.

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.

examples.text: Guarda la caja bajo llave.
examples.trans: Keep the box under lock and key.

meanings.note: Used both for a serving tray and an oven baking tray (bandeja de horno).

examples.text: Saca la bandeja dorada del horno con cuidado.
examples.trans: Take the golden tray out of the oven carefully.

examples.text: Clara lleva cuatro tazas de té en la bandeja.
examples.trans: Clara carries four cups of tea on the tray.

meanings.note: In baking, la base de la tarta means 'the pastry crust / base'.

examples.text: La base de almendra queda dorada y muy crujiente.
examples.trans: The almond crust turns out golden and very crisp.

examples.text: Ponemos una base de fieltro bajo las patas.
examples.trans: We put a felt base under the legs.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.text: Es una pieza caliente.
examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Fragrant baking spice.

examples.text: La canela es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The cinnamon is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la canela.
examples.trans: We talk about the cinnamon.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Faltan cinco minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is five minutes to twelve.

examples.text: Tenemos cinco mesas en el patio.
examples.trans: We have five tables in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuento).

examples.text: Mi abuela cuenta historias preciosas.
examples.trans: My grandmother tells lovely stories.

examples.text: Conté doce tazas en el armario.
examples.trans: I counted twelve cups in the cupboard.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de cuarenta minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in forty minutes.

examples.text: Son las seis y cuarenta y cinco.
examples.trans: It is six forty-five.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Tenemos cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: ¿Cuántos bizcochos puedes hornear?
examples.trans: How many sponge cakes can you bake?

examples.text: ¿Cuánto tiempo tenemos antes de las doce?
examples.trans: How much time do we have before twelve?

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Built from delante ('in front'), because an apron hangs down the front of the body.

examples.text: Rocío se ata el delantal limpio antes de encender el horno.
examples.trans: Rocio ties on her clean apron before turning on the oven.

examples.text: Colgamos los delantales blancos detrás de la puerta de la cocina.
examples.trans: We hung the white aprons behind the kitchen door.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine; los dulces = sweets/pastries.

examples.text: Es una pieza dulce.
examples.trans: It is a sweet piece.

examples.text: ¿Podemos servir mantequilla salada con mermelada dulce de fresa?
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with sweet strawberry jam?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Written as one word in modern Spanish.

examples.text: Subo el desayuno enseguida.
examples.trans: I will bring breakfast up right away.

examples.text: Enseguida vuelvo con la llave.
examples.trans: I will be right back with the key.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.text: La esquina está aquí.
examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

estuche.gloss: case (for an instrument, glasses, or pens)

meanings.en: case (for an instrument, glasses, or pens)
meanings.note: Used for fitted protective cases: estuche del violín, estuche de las gafas.

examples.text: Abrió con cuidado el estuche negro de su violín.
examples.trans: He carefully opened the black case of his violin.

examples.text: Siempre guardo las gafas de leer dentro de su estuche.
examples.trans: I always keep my reading glasses inside their case.

meanings.note: Invariable in singular (esquinas extra).

examples.text: Es una pieza extra.
examples.trans: It is an extra piece.

examples.text: Recién salido del horno: ¡bizcocho de limón de los viernes con esquinas extra!
examples.trans: Fresh from the oven: Friday lemon cake with extra corner pieces!

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera esta mañana.
examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Diminutive of golpe ('blow, knock'); dar golpecitos = to tap lightly.

examples.text: Dio dos golpecitos suaves en la puerta antes de entrar.
examples.trans: She gave two gentle taps on the door before coming in.

examples.text: El músico dio unos golpecitos en el atril para pedir silencio.
examples.trans: The musician tapped the music stand lightly to ask for quiet.

guardar.gloss: to keep; to put away; to guard

meanings.en: to keep; to put away; to guard
meanings.note: Everyday verb for putting something safely away in a pocket or cupboard.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en este cajón.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in this drawer.

examples.text: Te guardé el último rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I saved the last cinnamon roll for you.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.text: La habitación está aquí.
examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Built from horno (oven).

examples.text: La panadera hornea bizcochos cada viernes.
examples.trans: The baker bakes sponge cakes every Friday.

examples.text: Esta mañana horneamos pan crujiente.
examples.trans: This morning we baked crusty bread.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.text: Las ventanas dan al jardín.
examples.trans: The windows face the garden.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las ocho.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.text: El limonero está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: Es una pieza limpia.
examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: El limón está aquí.
examples.trans: The lemon is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemons from the door.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Nada mal = not bad at all; menos mal = thank goodness.

examples.text: Nada mal para el primer día.
examples.trans: Not bad at all for the first day.

examples.text: ¡Menos mal que trajiste paraguas!
examples.trans: Thank goodness you brought an umbrella!

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

meanings.note: Por lo menos = at least; echar de menos = to miss; a menos que = unless.

examples.text: Son las ocho menos diez.
examples.trans: It is ten to eight.

examples.text: Por lo menos ya no llueve.
examples.trans: At least it is no longer raining.

meanings.note: Té de menta = mint tea.

examples.text: La menta es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The mint is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la menta.
examples.trans: We talk about the mint.

meanings.note: Dining, cafe, or courtyard table.

examples.text: La mesa está aquí.
examples.trans: The table is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mesas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the tables from the door.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: En cinco minutos = in five minutes.

examples.text: El minuto está aquí.
examples.trans: The minute is here.

examples.text: Vemos los minutos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the minutes from the door.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Las nueve = nine o'clock.

examples.text: El tren llega a las nueve en punto.
examples.trans: The train arrives at nine on the dot.

examples.text: Vimos un nueve sobre diez.
examples.trans: We saw a nine out of ten.

meanings.note: Written after street names in Spanish addresses (Calle Mayor número ocho).

examples.text: El número está aquí.
examples.trans: The number is here.

examples.text: Vemos los números desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the numbers from the door.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Refers to dinner plates, teacup saucers, and cooked courses.

examples.text: Coloca cada taza blanca sobre su plato limpio.
examples.trans: Set each white cup on its clean saucer.

examples.text: La sopa caliente es el mejor plato para la lluvia.
examples.trans: Hot soup is the best dish for rainy weather.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.text: ¡Hasta pronto y buen viaje!
examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.text: Solo quedan dos habitaciones libres.
examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Llevo quince años en esta posada.
examples.trans: I have spent fifteen years at this inn.

examples.text: Dame quince minutos nada más.
examples.trans: Give me just fifteen minutes.

meanings.note: Baked pastry roll or scroll.

examples.text: El rollo está aquí.
examples.trans: The roll is here.

examples.text: Vemos los rollos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rolls from the door.

meanings.note: Sala de conciertos = concert hall; sala de la caldera = boiler room.

examples.text: La sala está aquí.
examples.trans: The hall is here.

examples.text: Vemos las salas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halls from the door.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el secreto), means 'secret'.

examples.text: Es una pieza secreta.
examples.trans: It is a secret piece.

examples.text: Claro, Mateo, ¡tu secreto está a salvo con nosotras!
examples.trans: Sure, Mateo, your secret is safe with us!

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: En silencio = quietly.

examples.text: El silencio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The silence is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el silencio.
examples.trans: We talk about the silence.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Built from té (tea).

examples.text: La tetera está aquí.
examples.trans: The teapot is here.

examples.text: Vemos las teteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teapots from the door.

meanings.note: Irregular: traigo, traje; future traeré.

examples.text: Ahora mismo le traigo una cuchara.
examples.trans: I will bring you a spoon right now.

examples.text: Ayer trajo flores del mercado.
examples.trans: Yesterday she brought flowers from the market.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.text: El trozo está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pieces from the door.

meanings.note: Accented té ('tea') distinguishes the noun from pronoun te ('you').

examples.text: El té está aquí.
examples.trans: The tea is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teas from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Contamos del uno al ocho.
examples.trans: We count from one to eight.

meanings.note: Feminine: la vecina.

examples.text: El vecino está aquí.
examples.trans: The neighbour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los vecinos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the neighbours from the door.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.text: Gracias por venir esta mañana.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.text: El viernes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent mark in the plural because -es makes it naturally stressed on -li-: los violines.

examples.text: Nuestro vecino toca el violín desde que tenía ocho años.
examples.trans: Our neighbour has played the violin since he was eight years old.

examples.text: El violín y el piano sonaron juntos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: The violin and the piano sounded together under the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.

examples.text: ¡Ya voy con las llaves!
examples.trans: Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Carries a written accent on ú.

examples.text: Es una pieza última.
examples.trans: It is a last piece.

examples.text: Diez, once, doce. Exacto hasta la última moneda. ¡Gracias!
examples.trans: Ten, eleven, twelve. Exact to the last coin. Thank you!
